title: Investigation 01: Microsoft Security Alert
subject: Two Microsoft Security Notifications
scenario:
EMAIL A
From: Microsoft 365 Security <no-reply@accountprotection.microsoft.com>
Subject: Unusual sign-in activity detected

We noticed a sign-in attempt from a new device. If this was you, no action is required. If you do not recognise this activity, visit your Microsoft account directly by typing the official address into your browser. We will never ask you to share your password or MFA code by email.

-----------------------------

EMAIL B
From: Microsoft 365 Security <security@micros0ft-account.example>
Subject: URGENT: Account Access Will Be Restricted

An unusual sign-in has been detected. Your account will be disabled in 15 minutes. Use the verification link below to restore access. You must provide your password and MFA code. Do not contact IT until verification is complete.

Verification link: https://micros0ft-login.example/verify
email_note: TASK: Compare both messages. Identify the legitimate Microsoft notification and the phishing email.
options: Email A is legitimate; Email B is phishing.
Email B is legitimate; Email A is phishing.
Both emails are legitimate.
Both emails are phishing.
explanation: Email A uses a Microsoft-owned account protection domain and directs users to access their account independently. Email B uses a lookalike domain, creates artificial urgency, requests passwords and MFA codes, and discourages contacting IT.
evidence_caption: Compare the sender, language and security instructions.

title: Investigation 02: HR Salary Revision
subject: Two Salary Revision Notifications
scenario:
EMAIL A
From: HR Department <hr@fujisilvertech.com>
Subject: Annual Salary Revision – Employee Notification

Dear Employee,

The annual salary revision process is underway. Employees can review their updated compensation details through the company's usual employee portal. For any clarification, contact HR through the official internal directory. Please do not share passwords or banking credentials by email.

-----------------------------

EMAIL B
From: Fuji Silvertech HR <hr@fujisilvertech-careers.example>
Subject: Confidential Salary Revision – Confirmation Required

Your revised salary will be released today. To avoid a delay, download the attached salary confirmation form and submit your employee ID, password and bank account details.

Portal: https://fujisilvertech.com
Actual destination: https://fujisilvertech-careers.example/salary
Reply-To: salary-confirm@external-mail.example

Failure to respond may postpone your salary revision.
email_note: TASK: Compare the two HR emails. Which one should employees trust?
options: Email A is legitimate; Email B is phishing.
Email B is legitimate; Email A is phishing.
Both emails are legitimate.
Both emails are phishing.
explanation: Email A uses the company email domain and directs employees to normal internal channels. Email B uses an unofficial domain, mismatched link destination, external Reply-To address and requests sensitive credentials and banking details.

title: Investigation 03: Supplier Invoice Manipulation
subject: Revised Beneficiary Details – Invoice INV-2026-1182
scenario:
Hello Finance Team,

Following our recent discussion, North Star Supplies has updated its banking arrangements. Please use the revised beneficiary details attached to settle invoice INV-2026-1182.

Beneficiary: North Star Supplies
Previous account: 4567891230
New account: 1234567890

The supplier has requested that this payment be completed before 4 PM to avoid a contractual penalty.

Management has already approved the change. To prevent duplication, please do not call the supplier using the number in your existing records. Use the new contact number provided in the attachment.

Please process this as a priority and reply once completed.

Regards,
Accounts Department
email_note: TASK: This message looks like a normal business request. Identify every suspicious instruction.

mistakes.text: Requests payment to a newly changed supplier bank account.
Creates urgency with a 4 PM payment deadline.
Claims management approval without independent verification.
Discourages calling the supplier using previously verified contact details.
Asks employees to use a new contact number supplied in the attachment.

explanation: This may be a business email compromise or invoice redirection attempt. A changed bank account must be verified through a previously trusted supplier contact. Never rely on contact details supplied in the same suspicious request.

title: Investigation 04: IT Helpdesk MFA Reset
subject: MFA Configuration Migration – Action Required
scenario:
Dear Employee,

As part of the scheduled identity platform migration, selected employee accounts require MFA re-registration.

To complete the process, follow the attached instructions:

1. Download and run MFA_Update.exe.
2. Scan the QR code in the document and sign in.
3. Approve the authentication notification when prompted.
4. Complete the process within 10 minutes to prevent temporary access restrictions.

If the notification appears more than once, approve the latest request to complete synchronisation.

Regards,
IT Service Desk
email_note: TASK: Investigate the technical instructions. Identify the suspicious elements.

mistakes.text: Sender uses an unverified company-support domain.
Requests an unexpected executable file named MFA_Update.exe.
Uses an unknown QR code to collect employee sign-in details.
Asks employees to approve unexpected MFA notifications.
Creates pressure with a 10-minute deadline and repeated approval instructions.

explanation: A legitimate IT migration should be confirmed through official internal channels. Unknown executable files, QR login links and unexpected MFA approval requests are serious warning signs. Never approve an authentication request you did not initiate.

title: The Confidential Client Report
subject: Client Report Sharing Request
scenario: You are preparing a confidential client report. A colleague from another department messages you requesting the complete report because they need a few figures for a presentation. They say their manager has already approved access. What should you do?
options: Send the report because they work in the same company.
Share only the pages they requested without checking.
Verify their access authorization and share through an approved channel.
Upload the report to a public file-sharing link.
explanation: Confidential client information should only be shared with authorised individuals who have a valid business need. Verify access and use approved company channels.

title: The Unattended Workstation
subject: Workstation Security
scenario: You are working on a client system when a colleague asks you to join a quick meeting in another room. You expect to return in two minutes. What is the correct action before leaving?
email_note: TASK: Select the correct workstation security practice.
options: Leave the screen open because you will return shortly.
Minimise all windows and leave the workstation unlocked.
Lock the workstation before leaving your desk.
Ask a colleague to watch your screen.
explanation: Always lock your workstation when leaving it unattended, even for a short period. This prevents unauthorised access to company systems and information.

title: The HR Benefits Announcement
subject: New Employee Benefits Update
scenario: You receive a message in a work group claiming that the company has introduced a new medical reimbursement benefit. It includes a form asking employees to enter personal details. The message has been forwarded several times, but there is no official announcement. What should you do?
email_note: TASK: Decide how to verify an internal company announcement.
options: Fill out the form before the benefit expires.
Forward the message to all colleagues.
Verify the announcement through official HR communication.
Enter only basic personal information to check the form.
explanation: Verify benefits, salary and policy announcements through official HR channels. Forwarded messages are not proof of authenticity, especially when they request personal information.

title: The Supplier Gift Offer
subject: Supplier Appreciation Gift
scenario: A supplier currently participating in a company contract offers you an expensive electronic device as a personal thank-you for helping their team. They ask you not to mention the gift because it is only a friendly gesture. What should you do?
email_note: TASK: Choose the most appropriate professional response.
options: Accept the gift because it is a personal gesture.
Accept it but keep it confidential.
Decline or disclose it according to company policy.
Ask the supplier to send it to your home.
explanation: Gifts from suppliers can create conflicts of interest or appear to influence business decisions. Follow the company's gift and hospitality policy and disclose the offer.

title: The Duplicate Payment Request
subject: Urgent: Possible Duplicate Invoice
scenario: A vendor calls saying that an invoice may have been paid twice. They request that you immediately send a refund to a different bank account to correct the issue. What should you do?
email_note: TASK: Identify the correct financial control.
options: Transfer the refund immediately to avoid a dispute.
Ask the caller to send another bank account by email.
Verify the payment records and follow the approved refund process.
Refund the amount using your own account temporarily.
explanation: Financial changes and refunds must be verified against official records and processed through approved finance controls. Never transfer funds based only on an unsolicited call.

title: The Executive Impersonation Test
subject: Confidential Request – Immediate Action
scenario: You receive an unexpected message that appears to come from a senior executive. They say they are in a confidential meeting and need you to purchase gift cards immediately. They ask you to send the codes directly and not discuss the request with anyone. What should you do?
email_note: TASK: Choose the safest response to a possible executive impersonation attempt.
options: Complete the purchase because the request came from management.
Send the codes first and verify later.
Verify the request through a separate trusted communication channel.
Forward the gift card codes to another employee.
explanation: Attackers may impersonate executives to create urgency and secrecy. Verify unusual financial or purchasing requests through a separate trusted channel before taking action.
